gap: No result ChatGPT got says that today (2026-11-08) on the makers' own US stores, all four big-brand headsets ChatGPT pushed cost more than $50: Logitech G435 $79.99, Logitech G321 $54.99, HyperX Cloud Jet $79.99 and Corsair HS55 Wireless $79.99. The only ones at maker price that are under $50 and have all three connections (2.4 GHz, Bluetooth and a 3.5 mm cable) are EKSA's E900 BT ($49.99, 20 ms, 50 h) and Mako BT ($39.99).
standout_why: I read SoundGuys' cheap-gaming-headset page, which ChatGPT cited. It gives the G435's MSRP as $79.99 next to a $34.48 Amazon price, does not mention the G321, Cloud Jet or any EKSA model, and its 'best wireless' pick is the $99.99 Arctis 1. RTINGS' wireless list (cited) and PC Gamer's list (cited) did not show their picks to my fetcher, and vaagame (cited) gave a certificate error, so I could not check those three. ChatGPT's own answers show the G435 at $79.99 at Walmart but say the Cloud Jet is $39.99–$47.99 at Best Buy. HyperX's own store lists the Cloud Jet at $79.99 with no sale price, and none of these pages gives a maker-store price for the Cloud Jet or the G321.
decides: It confirms our pick. At maker list price, no big-brand wireless headset fits under $50 today: the closest is the G321 at $54.99, and it has no cable mode. ChatGPT's top pick in the third chat, the HyperX Cloud Jet, is under $50 only through a retailer sale I could not check. So among headsets priced under $50 at the maker, the EKSA E900 BT ($49.99, 2.4 GHz at 20 ms + Bluetooth + 3.5 mm cable, 50 h) is still the strongest pick, and the Mako BT ($39.99) is the cheaper option with the same three connections.
